# Plan 3 — Agentic loop + tools + main system prompt

Authoritative spec: `mediator-bot-spec.md`. Read it in prep, paying special attention to: "The Five Knowledge Primitives", "Tools", "Agentic Loop", "Hot Context", "Prompts" (main system prompt section), "Stance on Assessments", "Frameworks the Assistant Borrows From", "Definitions", "In-Person Redirection", "Multi-Message Handling", and the "Stance" guidance.

Plans 1 and 2 are assumed complete: schema, config, DB, webhook ingestion, media pipeline, send_outbound. The interface contract `run_agentic_turn(triggering_message_ids, user)` was defined as a stub in Plan 2 — fill it in.

## Scope (in)
### Hot context builder
- `build_hot_context(current_user)` returns a structured object with: both users' profiles + style notes, all active OOB entries with severity, active memories about both users, active themes (titles + 1-line status, max ~10, weighted by recency), open watch items relevant to current user, active observations with significance ≥ 3, last ~20 messages in current user's thread (including prior assistant messages), time gap since last message, trigger metadata.
- The output shape is what gets injected into the LLM call. Use careful token budgeting — keep hot context under a sensible cap (~6k tokens) so cold retrieval via tools is the path for everything else.

### System prompt
- Single mega-prompt, stored as a versioned constant (`SYSTEM_PROMPT_V1`). Includes everything the spec lists: role, identity placeholder for assistant name, operating principles, Definitions section verbatim (crisis, charge levels, confidence, theme abstraction level, watch-item "addressed"), Stance on Assessments, the Five-Primitive Decision Framework with discriminators and examples, OOB rules and severity handling + countersummary language guidance, tool usage philosophy, per-tool guidance (when to use / when not to / examples), multi-message handling rules, in-person redirection triggers, crisis handling, refusal patterns, output style (WhatsApp-conversational, warm, brief), silence acceptable + must justify on charged messages, deliberate-relay handling.
- The OOB guardrail and check_oob behavior are referenced but the actual implementation is Plan 4 — system prompt should reflect the final intended behavior.

### Tools
Implement all tools listed in the spec's "Tools" section. Each is an async Python function callable by the loop, with strict argument validation (Pydantic models). The Pydantic input/output shapes are pre-defined in `tool_schemas.py` in the project root — use them as the single source of truth for argument validation and Anthropic tool-list rendering. Do not redefine tool shapes inline.

**Dedup via agentic search.** Write tools (`add_memory`, `log_observation`, etc.) do NOT have embedding-based or similarity-based dedup gates. The agent is responsible for reading existing rows via the corresponding read tool (`get_memories`, `get_observations`) before writing, and choosing add vs update vs supersede explicitly. The system prompt MUST include explicit guidance on this: "search existing memories/observations before writing; reinforcing an existing observation is `update_observation`, not a new `log_observation`." Do not add a vector store, embedding column, or similarity threshold anywhere.

Read tools (log to app logs only):
- `search_messages(partner?, date_range?, text_contains?)`
- `recent_activity(days)`
- `list_themes(active_only?, sort_by?)`, `get_theme(theme_id)`
- `get_memories(about_user_id?, status?, theme_id?)`
- `list_watch_items(owner_user_id?, status?)`
- `get_observations(theme_id?, status?, about_user_id?, min_significance?)`
- `get_oob(owner_id?)`
- `check_oob(content, recipient_id)` — placeholder that returns `{verdict: 'ok'}` until Plan 4 replaces it. Loop must call it on every outbound.
- `get_self_model(user_id)`
- `get_bot_actions(date_range?, target_type?)`

Write tools (log every call to `tool_calls`):
- `update_user_style_notes(user_id, notes)`
- `add_memory`, `update_memory`, `supersede_memory(old_id, new_content)`
- `create_theme`, `update_theme(theme_id, ...)`
- `add_watch_item`, `update_watch_item`, `address_watch_item(id, addressing_note)`
- `log_observation`, `update_observation`
- `add_oob`, `update_oob`, `lift_oob(oob_id)`
- `schedule_checkin(when, about_what, reason)` — supersedes any existing pending check-in for that user (Plan 5 fires it; here just write the row)
- `cancel_scheduled_checkin(user_id)`
- `escalate_to_partner(content, reason)` — logs distinctly; actual cross-partner outbound flow lands here (uses `send_outbound` from Plan 2 with the `escalation` template)
- `log_feedback(from_user_id, target_type, target_id, sentiment, content)`

Each write tool inserts a `tool_calls` row with `turn_id`, `tool_name`, `arguments`, `result`, `called_at`, `duration_ms`.

### The loop
Per-turn flow exactly per spec: orient → read (multiple rounds) → decide → respond (passes through `check_oob` placeholder) → write (using the five-primitive framework — multiple primitives can apply to one piece of info) → schedule (one follow-up check-in or none) → end turn.

**No hard cap on tool calls or wallclock per turn.** Daily LLM spend caps (Plan 1) are the budgetary backstop. `bot_turns` records `tool_call_count` and turn duration so admin (Plan 6) can spot pathological loops, but nothing terminates the loop early.

- Use Anthropic SDK with Claude Sonnet (latest at build time — read the runtime config; default to `claude-sonnet-4-6`). Use the SDK's native tool-use loop or equivalent.
- Prompt caching: cache the system prompt + tool definitions block. Cache hot context too if it's large enough to benefit.
- Open a `bot_turns` row at the start with `prompt_snapshot`, `triggered_by_message_id`, `user_in_context`, `started_at`, `model_version`. Update `final_output_message_id`, `reasoning`, `completed_at` at end. On error, set `failure_reason`.
- For "what did you do" queries the user might raise (e.g., "why did you tell her that?"), the loop should call `get_bot_actions` rather than relying on memory.
- Silence is a valid output. For charged messages, the loop must record a justification in `bot_turns.reasoning`.

### Significance scoring hook
- The `log_observation` tool accepts an optional `significance` argument the loop can pass directly. If absent, call a stub `score_observation(content, context) -> int` that returns 3 for now. Plan 4 replaces the stub with the real Haiku-based scorer.
- Store `scoring_prompt_version` alongside (string constant for now, e.g. `"v0-stub"`).

### Crisis handling (in-prompt)
- The system prompt instructs the model to drop the mediator role on crisis, surface resources, and call `escalate_to_partner` only at the high bar described.
- The actual escalation outbound uses the `escalation` template from Plan 2.

## Scope (out, deliberately)
- Real OOB checker LLM call (Plan 4 — `check_oob` here is a pass-through).
- Real significance scoring (Plan 4 — stub returns 3).
- Scheduled-job firing and decay (Plan 5).
- Pause/resume gating (Plan 5 — but the loop checks `paused_for_user(user_id)` before doing anything; Plan 2 stubbed it to False).
- Admin view, onboarding welcome, feedback (Plan 6).

## Success criteria
- `must`: An end-to-end test sends a mock inbound, the loop runs, an outbound is generated, `bot_turns` and any relevant `tool_calls` are written, and the outbound passes through `check_oob` (currently pass-through) before `send_outbound`.
- `must`: All 25+ tools defined, callable, schema-validated. Write tools log to `tool_calls`.
- `must`: Hot context is built from real DB state and kept under the configured token budget.
- `must`: System prompt embeds Definitions, Five-Primitive Framework, and stance guidance verbatim.
- `should`: Prompt caching is configured; observed cache hit on repeat calls in tests.
- `should`: A "why did you tell her that?" test query causes the loop to call `get_bot_actions`.
- `should`: A crisis-flagged message causes the loop to drop into supportive mode and consider `escalate_to_partner` (test uses a deterministic mock LLM if needed).
- `info`: Token budgets and model choice are documented.

## Notes
- Use `claude-sonnet-4-6` for the conversational loop. The prompt-caching block should include the system prompt + tools.
- Do NOT use diagnostic/clinical language anywhere in the prompt or outputs.
- The five primitives co-exist — the prompt must guide the model to write to multiple primitives when info fits more than one.

      "description": "Implement Anthropic tool-use loop integration inside `app/services/agentic.py` (or a new `app/services/llm.py` imported by agentic). Function shape: `async def run_phase(client, ctx, system_prompt, hot_context_rendered, allowed_tools, seed_messages) -> tuple[str, list[dict], int]` returning `(final_assistant_text, conversation_messages, tool_call_count)`.\n\nRequest construction (Phase A and reused for Phase B with caching):\n- `system` = two blocks: `[{\"type\":\"text\",\"text\":SYSTEM_PROMPT,\"cache_control\":{\"type\":\"ephemeral\"}}, {\"type\":\"text\",\"text\":hot_context_rendered}]` \u2014 second block gets `cache_control={\"type\":\"ephemeral\"}` ONLY when its estimated tokens (`len // 4`) \u2265 1024.\n- `tools = to_anthropic_tools(allowed_tools)`; mark the LAST entry with `cache_control={\"type\":\"ephemeral\"}`.\n- Phase A `messages` = `[{role:'user', content: f'Trigger: ids={ctx.triggering_message_ids} charge={charge}. Phase A: read what you need, then produce your user-facing reply as plain text.'}]`.\n- Phase B reuses the SAME `system` blocks (cache hit benefits A\u2192B same turn) and a different seed message (see T9 step 10).\n\nLoop body: while `stop_reason == 'tool_use'`, walk each `tool_use` block, call `await call_tool(name, args, ctx)`, append `tool_result` blocks (with `is_error=True` on validation errors), re-invoke `client.messages.create`. NO iteration cap.\n\nSpend cap + recording (FLAG-003/scope):\n- BEFORE each `client.messages.create`: `if not await is_under_cap(pool, 'text'): raise SpendCapExceeded`.\n- AFTER each successful response, compute dollars from `response.usage`:\n```python\nin_tok = usage.input_tokens; cache_create = usage.cache_creation_input_tokens or 0\ncache_read = usage.cache_read_input_tokens or 0; out_tok = usage.output_tokens\ndollars = ((in_tok - cache_create - cache_read) * input_price\n          + cache_create * input_price * 1.25\n          + cache_read * input_price * 0.10\n          + out_tok * output_price) / 1_000_000\nawait record_llm_cost(pool, 'text', dollars)\n```\nOn `SpendCapExceeded`: stamp `failure_reason='spend_cap'` and abort phase.\n\nErrors: retry once on transient errors. On persistent failure during phase A for `charge in ('charged','crisis')`: send `\"I'm having trouble responding right now, give me a moment\"` (free-form within window, otherwise `checkin_nudge` template), set `failure_reason='llm_timeout'`, skip phase B. For routine: queue silently.\n\nReasoning capture: any text content in phase A that PRECEDES the final assistant text is collected and appended to `bot_turns.reasoning`; phase B text content (annotations/thoughts) is also appended.",

  "meta_commentary": "Plan 3 has three high-risk gotchas the executor must internalize before writing any code:\n\n(1) **Escalation gate ordering (FLAG-005)**: the original plan text described `send_outbound(...)` BEFORE the gate check. The executor must invert this \u2014 gate FIRST, then send. T5 spells it out and T11.7 is the contract test. Sending before gating would let any model invocation trigger an unauthorized partner outbound.\n\n(2) **tool_call_count semantics (FLAG-007)**: the original plan text expected `tool_call_count == 3` (writes only). The spec wants admin visibility into pathological loops, so it must be the total across both phases (reads + writes). T13.1 expects 6.\n\n(3) **Two-phase dedup tension (FLAG-006)**: Phase B has NO read tools. The model cannot search-before-write mid-phase-B. The system prompt must therefore tell the model 'do all reads in phase A, even ones that only inform writes' so the read context carries forward via the conversation transcript into phase B. This is a non-obvious constraint that needs explicit prompt text.\n\n**Build order**: Phase 1 (T1, T2) \u2192 Phase 2 (T3 \u2192 T4 \u2192 T5 \u2192 T6) \u2192 Phase 3 (T7) \u2192 hooks (T8) \u2192 Phase 4 (T9 \u2192 T10) \u2192 Tests (T11, T12, T13) \u2192 run suite (T14). T8 has no deps and can run any time. T7 depends only on T1+T3, so it can run in parallel with T4\u2013T6.\n\n**File layout**: prefer `app/services/tools/` package (read_tools.py, write_tools.py, registry.py, __init__.py). Keep each under ~400 lines.\n\n**Dispatch must be registry-driven**, not a giant if/elif tree. `TOOL_DISPATCH` and `TOOL_DESCRIPTIONS` are dict lookups. New tools added by editing the dict, not the dispatcher.\n\n**Phase A messages \u2192 Phase B**: phase B inherits the entire phase A conversation history (assistant turns + tool_use + tool_result blocks). Append the synthetic 'You sent: ...' user message and switch tools to WRITE_PHASE_TOOLS. The cached system prompt blocks stay valid across A\u2192B in the same turn (this is the cache hit benefit).\n\n**Spend recording**: must happen on EVERY successful response, including responses that only contain tool_use (no final text). The cap check + record_llm_cost wraps each `client.messages.create` call inside the loop, not just once per phase.\n\n**Hot context built BEFORE bot_turns row**: this is non-obvious. The original plan text opened `bot_turns` first and built hot context after \u2014 but `prompt_snapshot` would then miss the hot context. T9 reorders this.\n\n**Existing test preservation**: `tests/test_send_outbound.py:15-19` has an autouse fixture that sets `hooks.check_oob = None`. That's intentional (it tests the no-hook path). Do NOT remove or modify that fixture. The new module-level pass-through default is for production and the new e2e test, not for existing send_outbound tests.\n\n**No new schema**: Plans 1+2 own all DB structure. (flagged 1 times across 1 plans)
- [DEBT] debouncer: debouncer: coalescer cannot satisfy the `run_agentic_turn(message_ids, user)` callback contract from an `add(user_id, message_id)` api unless it stores or resolves the user object. (flagged 1 times across 1 plans)
- [DEBT] did-the-work-fully-address-the-issue-hints-user-notes-and-approved-plan-requirements: did the work fully address the issue hints, user notes, and approved plan requirements?: checked the search-before-write requirement against the new phase split. because phase b exposes only write/schedule tools, the model cannot recover by calling `get_memories`, `get_observations`, or `list_themes` if it realizes during phase b that it lacks enough read context to safely add versus update; this creates tension with the explicit agentic-search dedup requirement.         Idea:
# Plan 3 — Agentic loop + tools + main system prompt

Authoritative spec: `mediator-bot-spec.md`. Read it in prep, paying special attention to: "The Five Knowledge Primitives", "Tools", "Agentic Loop", "Hot Context", "Prompts" (main system prompt section), "Stance on Assessments", "Frameworks the Assistant Borrows From", "Definitions", "In-Person Redirection", "Multi-Message Handling", and the "Stance" guidance.

Plans 1 and 2 are assumed complete: schema, config, DB, webhook ingestion, media pipeline, send_outbound. The interface contract `run_agentic_turn(triggering_message_ids, user)` was defined as a stub in Plan 2 — fill it in.

## Scope (in)
### Hot context builder
- `build_hot_context(current_user)` returns a structured object with: both users' profiles + style notes, all active OOB entries with severity, active memories about both users, active themes (titles + 1-line status, max ~10, weighted by recency), open watch items relevant to current user, active observations with significance ≥ 3, last ~20 messages in current user's thread (including prior assistant messages), time gap since last message, trigger metadata.
- The output shape is what gets injected into the LLM call. Use careful token budgeting — keep hot context under a sensible cap (~6k tokens) so cold retrieval via tools is the path for everything else.

### System prompt
- Single mega-prompt, stored as a versioned constant (`SYSTEM_PROMPT_V1`). Includes everything the spec lists: role, identity placeholder for assistant name, operating principles, Definitions section verbatim (crisis, charge levels, confidence, theme abstraction level, watch-item "addressed"), Stance on Assessments, the Five-Primitive Decision Framework with discriminators and examples, OOB rules and severity handling + countersummary language guidance, tool usage philosophy, per-tool guidance (when to use / when not to / examples), multi-message handling rules, in-person redirection triggers, crisis handling, refusal patterns, output style (WhatsApp-conversational, warm, brief), silence acceptable + must justify on charged messages, deliberate-relay handling.
- The OOB guardrail and check_oob behavior are referenced but the actual implementation is Plan 4 — system prompt should reflect the final intended behavior.

### Tools
Implement all tools listed in the spec's "Tools" section. Each is an async Python function callable by the loop, with strict argument validation (Pydantic models). The Pydantic input/output shapes are pre-defined in `tool_schemas.py` in the project root — use them as the single source of truth for argument validation and Anthropic tool-list rendering. Do not redefine tool shapes inline.

**Dedup via agentic search.** Write tools (`add_memory`, `log_observation`, etc.) do NOT have embedding-based or similarity-based dedup gates. The agent is responsible for reading existing rows via the corresponding read tool (`get_memories`, `get_observations`) before writing, and choosing add vs update vs supersede explicitly. The system prompt MUST include explicit guidance on this: "search existing memories/observations before writing; reinforcing an existing observation is `update_observation`, not a new `log_observation`." Do not add a vector store, embedding column, or similarity threshold anywhere.

Read tools (log to app logs only):
- `search_messages(partner?, date_range?, text_contains?)`
- `recent_activity(days)`
- `list_themes(active_only?, sort_by?)`, `get_theme(theme_id)`
- `get_memories(about_user_id?, status?, theme_id?)`
- `list_watch_items(owner_user_id?, status?)`
- `get_observations(theme_id?, status?, about_user_id?, min_significance?)`
- `get_oob(owner_id?)`
- `check_oob(content, recipient_id)` — placeholder that returns `{verdict: 'ok'}` until Plan 4 replaces it. Loop must call it on every outbound.
- `get_self_model(user_id)`
- `get_bot_actions(date_range?, target_type?)`

Write tools (log every call to `tool_calls`):
- `update_user_style_notes(user_id, notes)`
- `add_memory`, `update_memory`, `supersede_memory(old_id, new_content)`
- `create_theme`, `update_theme(theme_id, ...)`
- `add_watch_item`, `update_watch_item`, `address_watch_item(id, addressing_note)`
- `log_observation`, `update_observation`
- `add_oob`, `update_oob`, `lift_oob(oob_id)`
- `schedule_checkin(when, about_what, reason)` — supersedes any existing pending check-in for that user (Plan 5 fires it; here just write the row)
- `cancel_scheduled_checkin(user_id)`
- `escalate_to_partner(content, reason)` — logs distinctly; actual cross-partner outbound flow lands here (uses `send_outbound` from Plan 2 with the `escalation` template)
- `log_feedback(from_user_id, target_type, target_id, sentiment, content)`

Each write tool inserts a `tool_calls` row with `turn_id`, `tool_name`, `arguments`, `result`, `called_at`, `duration_ms`.

### The loop
Per-turn flow exactly per spec: orient → read (multiple rounds) → decide → respond (passes through `check_oob` placeholder) → write (using the five-primitive framework — multiple primitives can apply to one piece of info) → schedule (one follow-up check-in or none) → end turn.

**No hard cap on tool calls or wallclock per turn.** Daily LLM spend caps (Plan 1) are the budgetary backstop. `bot_turns` records `tool_call_count` and turn duration so admin (Plan 6) can spot pathological loops, but nothing terminates the loop early.

- Use Anthropic SDK with Claude Sonnet (latest at build time — read the runtime config; default to `claude-sonnet-4-6`). Use the SDK's native tool-use loop or equivalent.
- Prompt caching: cache the system prompt + tool definitions block. Cache hot context too if it's large enough to benefit.
- Open a `bot_turns` row at the start with `prompt_snapshot`, `triggered_by_message_id`, `user_in_context`, `started_at`, `model_version`. Update `final_output_message_id`, `reasoning`, `completed_at` at end. On error, set `failure_reason`.
- For "what did you do" queries the user might raise (e.g., "why did you tell her that?"), the loop should call `get_bot_actions` rather than relying on memory.
- Silence is a valid output. For charged messages, the loop must record a justification in `bot_turns.reasoning`.

### Significance scoring hook
- The `log_observation` tool accepts an optional `significance` argument the loop can pass directly. If absent, call a stub `score_observation(content, context) -> int` that returns 3 for now. Plan 4 replaces the stub with the real Haiku-based scorer.
- Store `scoring_prompt_version` alongside (string constant for now, e.g. `"v0-stub"`).

### Crisis handling (in-prompt)
- The system prompt instructs the model to drop the mediator role on crisis, surface resources, and call `escalate_to_partner` only at the high bar described.
- The actual escalation outbound uses the `escalation` template from Plan 2.

## Scope (out, deliberately)
- Real OOB checker LLM call (Plan 4 — `check_oob` here is a pass-through).
- Real significance scoring (Plan 4 — stub returns 3).
- Scheduled-job firing and decay (Plan 5).
- Pause/resume gating (Plan 5 — but the loop checks `paused_for_user(user_id)` before doing anything; Plan 2 stubbed it to False).
- Admin view, onboarding welcome, feedback (Plan 6).

## Success criteria
- `must`: An end-to-end test sends a mock inbound, the loop runs, an outbound is generated, `bot_turns` and any relevant `tool_calls` are written, and the outbound passes through `check_oob` (currently pass-through) before `send_outbound`.
- `must`: All 25+ tools defined, callable, schema-validated. Write tools log to `tool_calls`.
- `must`: Hot context is built from real DB state and kept under the configured token budget.
- `must`: System prompt embeds Definitions, Five-Primitive Framework, and stance guidance verbatim.
- `should`: Prompt caching is configured; observed cache hit on repeat calls in tests.
- `should`: A "why did you tell her that?" test query causes the loop to call `get_bot_actions`.
- `should`: A crisis-flagged message causes the loop to drop into supportive mode and consider `escalate_to_partner` (test uses a deterministic mock LLM if needed).
- `info`: Token budgets and model choice are documented.

## Notes
- Use `claude-sonnet-4-6` for the conversational loop. The prompt-caching block should include the system prompt + tools.
- Do NOT use diagnostic/clinical language anywhere in the prompt or outputs.
- The five primitives co-exist — the prompt must guide the model to write to multiple primitives when info fits more than one.

      "id": "T10",
      "description": "Implement Anthropic tool-use loop integration inside `app/services/agentic.py` (or a new `app/services/llm.py` imported by agentic). Function shape: `async def run_phase(client, ctx, system_prompt, hot_context_rendered, allowed_tools, seed_messages) -> tuple[str, list[dict], int]` returning `(final_assistant_text, conversation_messages, tool_call_count)`.\n\nRequest construction (Phase A and reused for Phase B with caching):\n- `system` = two blocks: `[{\"type\":\"text\",\"text\":SYSTEM_PROMPT,\"cache_control\":{\"type\":\"ephemeral\"}}, {\"type\":\"text\",\"text\":hot_context_rendered}]` \u2014 second block gets `cache_control={\"type\":\"ephemeral\"}` ONLY when its estimated tokens (`len // 4`) \u2265 1024.\n- `tools = to_anthropic_tools(allowed_tools)`; mark the LAST entry with `cache_control={\"type\":\"ephemeral\"}`.\n- Phase A `messages` = `[{role:'user', content: f'Trigger: ids={ctx.triggering_message_ids} charge={charge}. Phase A: read what you need, then produce your user-facing reply as plain text.'}]`.\n- Phase B reuses the SAME `system` blocks (cache hit benefits A\u2192B same turn) and a different seed message (see T9 step 10).\n\nLoop body: while `stop_reason == 'tool_use'`, walk each `tool_use` block, call `await call_tool(name, args, ctx)`, append `tool_result` blocks (with `is_error=True` on validation errors), re-invoke `client.messages.create`. NO iteration cap.\n\nSpend cap + recording (FLAG-003/scope):\n- BEFORE each `client.messages.create`: `if not await is_under_cap(pool, 'text'): raise SpendCapExceeded`.\n- AFTER each successful response, compute dollars from `response.usage`:\n```python\nin_tok = usage.input_tokens; cache_create = usage.cache_creation_input_tokens or 0\ncache_read = usage.cache_read_input_tokens or 0; out_tok = usage.output_tokens\ndollars = ((in_tok - cache_create - cache_read) * input_price\n          + cache_create * input_price * 1.25\n          + cache_read * input_price * 0.10\n          + out_tok * output_price) / 1_000_000\nawait record_llm_cost(pool, 'text', dollars)\n```\nOn `SpendCapExceeded`: stamp `failure_reason='spend_cap'` and abort phase.\n\nErrors: retry once on transient errors. On persistent failure during phase A for `charge in ('charged','crisis')`: send `\"I'm having trouble responding right now, give me a moment\"` (free-form within window, otherwise `checkin_nudge` template), set `failure_reason='llm_timeout'`, skip phase B. For routine: queue silently.\n\nReasoning capture: any text content in phase A that PRECEDES the final assistant text is collected and appended to `bot_turns.reasoning`; phase B text content (annotations/thoughts) is also appended.",

        Idea:
# Plan 3 — Agentic loop + tools + main system prompt

Authoritative spec: `mediator-bot-spec.md`. Read it in prep, paying special attention to: "The Five Knowledge Primitives", "Tools", "Agentic Loop", "Hot Context", "Prompts" (main system prompt section), "Stance on Assessments", "Frameworks the Assistant Borrows From", "Definitions", "In-Person Redirection", "Multi-Message Handling", and the "Stance" guidance.

Plans 1 and 2 are assumed complete: schema, config, DB, webhook ingestion, media pipeline, send_outbound. The interface contract `run_agentic_turn(triggering_message_ids, user)` was defined as a stub in Plan 2 — fill it in.

## Scope (in)
### Hot context builder
- `build_hot_context(current_user)` returns a structured object with: both users' profiles + style notes, all active OOB entries with severity, active memories about both users, active themes (titles + 1-line status, max ~10, weighted by recency), open watch items relevant to current user, active observations with significance ≥ 3, last ~20 messages in current user's thread (including prior assistant messages), time gap since last message, trigger metadata.
- The output shape is what gets injected into the LLM call. Use careful token budgeting — keep hot context under a sensible cap (~6k tokens) so cold retrieval via tools is the path for everything else.

### System prompt
- Single mega-prompt, stored as a versioned constant (`SYSTEM_PROMPT_V1`). Includes everything the spec lists: role, identity placeholder for assistant name, operating principles, Definitions section verbatim (crisis, charge levels, confidence, theme abstraction level, watch-item "addressed"), Stance on Assessments, the Five-Primitive Decision Framework with discriminators and examples, OOB rules and severity handling + countersummary language guidance, tool usage philosophy, per-tool guidance (when to use / when not to / examples), multi-message handling rules, in-person redirection triggers, crisis handling, refusal patterns, output style (WhatsApp-conversational, warm, brief), silence acceptable + must justify on charged messages, deliberate-relay handling.
- The OOB guardrail and check_oob behavior are referenced but the actual implementation is Plan 4 — system prompt should reflect the final intended behavior.

### Tools
Implement all tools listed in the spec's "Tools" section. Each is an async Python function callable by the loop, with strict argument validation (Pydantic models). The Pydantic input/output shapes are pre-defined in `tool_schemas.py` in the project root — use them as the single source of truth for argument validation and Anthropic tool-list rendering. Do not redefine tool shapes inline.

**Dedup via agentic search.** Write tools (`add_memory`, `log_observation`, etc.) do NOT have embedding-based or similarity-based dedup gates. The agent is responsible for reading existing rows via the corresponding read tool (`get_memories`, `get_observations`) before writing, and choosing add vs update vs supersede explicitly. The system prompt MUST include explicit guidance on this: "search existing memories/observations before writing; reinforcing an existing observation is `update_observation`, not a new `log_observation`." Do not add a vector store, embedding column, or similarity threshold anywhere.

Read tools (log to app logs only):
- `search_messages(partner?, date_range?, text_contains?)`
- `recent_activity(days)`
- `list_themes(active_only?, sort_by?)`, `get_theme(theme_id)`
- `get_memories(about_user_id?, status?, theme_id?)`
- `list_watch_items(owner_user_id?, status?)`
- `get_observations(theme_id?, status?, about_user_id?, min_significance?)`
- `get_oob(owner_id?)`
- `check_oob(content, recipient_id)` — placeholder that returns `{verdict: 'ok'}` until Plan 4 replaces it. Loop must call it on every outbound.
- `get_self_model(user_id)`
- `get_bot_actions(date_range?, target_type?)`

Write tools (log every call to `tool_calls`):
- `update_user_style_notes(user_id, notes)`
- `add_memory`, `update_memory`, `supersede_memory(old_id, new_content)`
- `create_theme`, `update_theme(theme_id, ...)`
- `add_watch_item`, `update_watch_item`, `address_watch_item(id, addressing_note)`
- `log_observation`, `update_observation`
- `add_oob`, `update_oob`, `lift_oob(oob_id)`
- `schedule_checkin(when, about_what, reason)` — supersedes any existing pending check-in for that user (Plan 5 fires it; here just write the row)
- `cancel_scheduled_checkin(user_id)`
- `escalate_to_partner(content, reason)` — logs distinctly; actual cross-partner outbound flow lands here (uses `send_outbound` from Plan 2 with the `escalation` template)
- `log_feedback(from_user_id, target_type, target_id, sentiment, content)`

Each write tool inserts a `tool_calls` row with `turn_id`, `tool_name`, `arguments`, `result`, `called_at`, `duration_ms`.

### The loop
Per-turn flow exactly per spec: orient → read (multiple rounds) → decide → respond (passes through `check_oob` placeholder) → write (using the five-primitive framework — multiple primitives can apply to one piece of info) → schedule (one follow-up check-in or none) → end turn.

**No hard cap on tool calls or wallclock per turn.** Daily LLM spend caps (Plan 1) are the budgetary backstop. `bot_turns` records `tool_call_count` and turn duration so admin (Plan 6) can spot pathological loops, but nothing terminates the loop early.

- Use Anthropic SDK with Claude Sonnet (latest at build time — read the runtime config; default to `claude-sonnet-4-6`). Use the SDK's native tool-use loop or equivalent.
- Prompt caching: cache the system prompt + tool definitions block. Cache hot context too if it's large enough to benefit.
- Open a `bot_turns` row at the start with `prompt_snapshot`, `triggered_by_message_id`, `user_in_context`, `started_at`, `model_version`. Update `final_output_message_id`, `reasoning`, `completed_at` at end. On error, set `failure_reason`.
- For "what did you do" queries the user might raise (e.g., "why did you tell her that?"), the loop should call `get_bot_actions` rather than relying on memory.
- Silence is a valid output. For charged messages, the loop must record a justification in `bot_turns.reasoning`.

### Significance scoring hook
- The `log_observation` tool accepts an optional `significance` argument the loop can pass directly. If absent, call a stub `score_observation(content, context) -> int` that returns 3 for now. Plan 4 replaces the stub with the real Haiku-based scorer.
- Store `scoring_prompt_version` alongside (string constant for now, e.g. `"v0-stub"`).

### Crisis handling (in-prompt)
- The system prompt instructs the model to drop the mediator role on crisis, surface resources, and call `escalate_to_partner` only at the high bar described.
- The actual escalation outbound uses the `escalation` template from Plan 2.

## Scope (out, deliberately)
- Real OOB checker LLM call (Plan 4 — `check_oob` here is a pass-through).
- Real significance scoring (Plan 4 — stub returns 3).
- Scheduled-job firing and decay (Plan 5).
- Pause/resume gating (Plan 5 — but the loop checks `paused_for_user(user_id)` before doing anything; Plan 2 stubbed it to False).
- Admin view, onboarding welcome, feedback (Plan 6).

## Success criteria
- `must`: An end-to-end test sends a mock inbound, the loop runs, an outbound is generated, `bot_turns` and any relevant `tool_calls` are written, and the outbound passes through `check_oob` (currently pass-through) before `send_outbound`.
- `must`: All 25+ tools defined, callable, schema-validated. Write tools log to `tool_calls`.
- `must`: Hot context is built from real DB state and kept under the configured token budget.
- `must`: System prompt embeds Definitions, Five-Primitive Framework, and stance guidance verbatim.
- `should`: Prompt caching is configured; observed cache hit on repeat calls in tests.
- `should`: A "why did you tell her that?" test query causes the loop to call `get_bot_actions`.
- `should`: A crisis-flagged message causes the loop to drop into supportive mode and consider `escalate_to_partner` (test uses a deterministic mock LLM if needed).
- `info`: Token budgets and model choice are documented.

## Notes
- Use `claude-sonnet-4-6` for the conversational loop. The prompt-caching block should include the system prompt + tools.

Returns `ScheduleCheckinOutput(job_id, superseded_job_id, scheduled_for)`.\n- `cancel_scheduled_checkin` (symmetric; returns `noop` if nothing pending).\n- **`escalate_to_partner` (CRITICAL ORDER FIX for FLAG-005/correctness-1):** ENFORCE THE GATE FIRST, then send. Step order: (1) override IDs server-side: `from_user_id := ctx.user.id`, `to_user_id := ctx.partner.id` (log warning if model passed mismatched IDs); (2) enforce gate: require `args.is_crisis is True` OR `args.reason` contains an explicit user-request marker \u2014 otherwise return a tool error to the LLM and DO NOT call `send_outbound`; (3) ONLY AFTER gate passes, construct `template = TemplateCall(name='escalation', params=[ctx.partner.name, ctx.user.name, args.content])` and `out_id = await send_outbound(ctx.pool, ctx.partner, args.content, template_fallback=template, bot_turn_id=ctx.turn_id)`; (4) append `f'\\nESCALATION: {args.reason}'` to `bot_turns.reasoning` (UPDATE).\n- `log_feedback` (straight insert).\nAlso define `SCORING_PROMPT_VERSION = 'v0-stub'` and `async def score_observation_stub(content: str, ctx: TurnContext) -> int: return 3` in this module.",

      "id": "T10",
      "description": "Implement Anthropic tool-use loop integration inside `app/services/agentic.py` (or a new `app/services/llm.py` imported by agentic). Function shape: `async def run_phase(client, ctx, system_prompt, hot_context_rendered, allowed_tools, seed_messages) -> tuple[str, list[dict], int]` returning `(final_assistant_text, conversation_messages, tool_call_count)`.\n\nRequest construction (Phase A and reused for Phase B with caching):\n- `system` = two blocks: `[{\"type\":\"text\",\"text\":SYSTEM_PROMPT,\"cache_control\":{\"type\":\"ephemeral\"}}, {\"type\":\"text\",\"text\":hot_context_rendered}]` \u2014 second block gets `cache_control={\"type\":\"ephemeral\"}` ONLY when its estimated tokens (`len // 4`) \u2265 1024.\n- `tools = to_anthropic_tools(allowed_tools)`; mark the LAST entry with `cache_control={\"type\":\"ephemeral\"}`.\n- Phase A `messages` = `[{role:'user', content: f'Trigger: ids={ctx.triggering_message_ids} charge={charge}. Phase A: read what you need, then produce your user-facing reply as plain text.'}]`.\n- Phase B reuses the SAME `system` blocks (cache hit benefits A\u2192B same turn) and a different seed message (see T9 step 10).\n\nLoop body: while `stop_reason == 'tool_use'`, walk each `tool_use` block, call `await call_tool(name, args, ctx)`, append `tool_result` blocks (with `is_error=True` on validation errors), re-invoke `client.messages.create`. NO iteration cap.\n\nSpend cap + recording (FLAG-003/scope):\n- BEFORE each `client.messages.create`: `if not await is_under_cap(pool, 'text'): raise SpendCapExceeded`.\n- AFTER each successful response, compute dollars from `response.usage`:\n```python\nin_tok = usage.input_tokens; cache_create = usage.cache_creation_input_tokens or 0\ncache_read = usage.cache_read_input_tokens or 0; out_tok = usage.output_tokens\ndollars = ((in_tok - cache_create - cache_read) * input_price\n          + cache_create * input_price * 1.25\n          + cache_read * input_price * 0.10\n          + out_tok * output_price) / 1_000_000\nawait record_llm_cost(pool, 'text', dollars)\n```\nOn `SpendCapExceeded`: stamp `failure_reason='spend_cap'` and abort phase.\n\nErrors: retry once on transient errors. On persistent failure during phase A for `charge in ('charged','crisis')`: send `\"I'm having trouble responding right now, give me a moment\"` (free-form within window, otherwise `checkin_nudge` template), set `failure_reason='llm_timeout'`, skip phase B. For routine: queue silently.\n\nReasoning capture: any text content in phase A that PRECEDES the final assistant text is collected and appended to `bot_turns.reasoning`; phase B text content (annotations/thoughts) is also appended.",

  "patch": "*** Begin Patch\n*** Add File: app/services/turn_context.py\n+\"\"\"Per-turn context shared by the agentic loop and tool implementations.\"\"\"\n+\n+from dataclasses import dataclass\n+from typing import Any, Literal\n+from uuid import UUID\n+\n+from app.models.user import User\n+\n+\n+@dataclass\n+class TurnContext:\n+    turn_id: UUID\n+    pool: Any\n+    user: User\n+    partner: User\n+    triggering_message_ids: list[UUID]\n+    phase: Literal[\"read\", \"write\"] = \"read\"\n+\n+\n+async def partner_of(pool: Any, user: User) -> User:\n+    rows = await pool.fetch(\n+        \"\"\"\n+        SELECT id, name, phone, timezone\n+        FROM users\n+        WHERE id <> $1\n+        \"\"\",\n+        user.id,\n+    )\n+    if len(rows) != 1:\n+        raise ValueError(f\"expected exactly one partner for user {user.id}, found {len(rows)}\")\n+    row = rows[0]\n+    return User(id=row[\"id\"], name=row[\"name\"], phone=row[\"phone\"], timezone=row[\"timezone\"])\n*** Add File: app/services/prompts.py\n+\"\"\"Versioned system prompts for the agentic conversational loop.\"\"\"\n+\n+SYSTEM_PROMPT_VERSION = \"v1\"\n+\n+SYSTEM_PROMPT_V1 = \"\"\"\n+# Role And Identity\n+\n+You are {assistant_name}, a relationship reflection and mediation assistant operating privately between two named partners: {partner_a_name} and {partner_b_name}.\n+\n+You are not a therapist. You help each partner reflect, translate charged content into hearable form, notice grounded patterns, protect explicit out-of-bounds boundaries, and redirect toward direct conversation when direct conversation is the better tool.\n+\n+# Operating Principles\n+\n+- Ground in data. Use hot context and tools before assuming.\n+- Distill, but quote when exact wording carries important information.\n+- Keep attribution clear. Say what came from the current user, what came from prior context, and what is your own tentative read.\n+- Default to transparency with explicit out-of-bounds exceptions.\n+- Treat both partners symmetrically. Do not become one partner's weapon or secret strategy engine.\n+- Hold uncertainty plainly. Observations are testable, not authoritative.\n+- Be useful in the current moment. Prefer one clear next move over a broad analysis.\n+\n+# Definitions\n+\n+Concrete definitions for terms used throughout the spec. The bot's prompts include these so behavior is consistent.\n+\n+**Crisis** — used to determine when the bot drops the mediator role:\n+- Signs of self-harm ideation or intent\n+- Signs of imminent danger to self or others\n+- Signs of abuse (emotional, physical, sexual)\n+- Severe acute distress (panic, dissociation, breakdown)\n+\n+Anything else, including intense relationship friction, is not crisis.\n+\n+**Message charge levels:**\n+- `routine` — everyday content, low emotional weight\n+- `notable` — emotionally meaningful but not heavy\n+- `charged` — significant emotional weight, conflict, vulnerability, or intensity\n+- `crisis` — meets crisis criteria above\n+\n+**Observation confidence:**\n+- `high` — multiple reinforcing instances over time, or directly stated by the partner\n+- `medium` — clear pattern with some evidence, but limited reinforcement\n+- `low` — initial impression, single instance, or speculative\n+\n+**Significance scoring (1-5)** — anchor examples in the Significance Scoring section.\n+\n+**Watch item \"addressed\"** — the bot has surfaced the item with the user, or the user has resolved it themselves, or the underlying situation has changed enough that the item no longer applies. The bot logs which case it was via the `addressing_note` parameter on `address_watch_item`.\n+\n+**Theme abstraction level** — themes are **life domains**, not specific topics or recurring arguments. See Themes below.\n+\n+# Stance On Assessments\n+\n+The assistant makes honest observations without inferring pathology. It does **not** use diagnostic or clinical language (\"anxious attachment,\" \"ADHD traits,\" \"avoidant\"). It **does** describe behavior and patterns clearly when they're grounded in data. Observations are held as testable, not authoritative — the assistant invites confirmation or pushback, treats both partners as capable adults, and avoids both flattering vagueness and pathologizing labels.\n+\n+# Frameworks The Assistant Borrows From\n+\n+The assistant is not a therapist and does not deliver therapy. It borrows lenses and techniques from established frameworks, applied with judgment:\n+\n+- **Nonviolent Communication (NVC)** — \"when X, I feel Y, because I need Z\" structure for translating charged content into hearable form\n+- **Gottman-style pattern recognition** — noticing bids, repair attempts, and the four horsemen (criticism, contempt, defensiveness, stonewalling) as observations, not diagnoses\n+- **Internal Family Systems \"parts\" language** — surfacing ambivalence without flattening it\n+- **Reflective listening** — paraphrasing before responding to confirm understanding\n+- **Curiosity over interpretation** — questions before diagnoses\n+- **Repair attempt surfacing** — naming de-escalation moves the recipient may have missed\n+- **Externalizing the problem** — framing recurring tensions as something the couple faces together\n+\n+These are tools, not modes. The assistant blends them based on what the moment calls for.\n+\n+# Five-Primitive Decision Framework\n+\n+The assistant accumulates structured understanding through five distinct primitives. Each has a clear role; write to whichever fits. When something fits more than one, write to all that apply — primitives are designed to coexist, not partition.\n+\n+1. Style notes — durable traits about how a person communicates and processes.\n+   - Use for a living summary of communication/process style.\n+   - Do not use for one-off facts or single incidents.\n+   - Example: \"Tends to understate when upset. Processes by talking it out, gets clearer through speech.\"\n+\n+2. Memories — specific facts about the people and their life.\n+   - Discriminator: Is it a fact? -> memory.\n+   - Link to themes when the fact sits within a life domain.\n+   - Example: \"They've been trying for a kid since January 2024.\"\n+\n+3. Themes — high-level life domains.\n+   - Discriminator: Is it a durable life domain organizing a category of experience? -> theme.\n+   - Themes are life domains, not specific topics or recurring arguments. Create them conservatively.\n+   - Examples: \"Caring for aging parents\"; \"Balancing work demands and the relationship\"; \"Physical intimacy and connection.\"\n+   - Not themes: \"weekend planning friction\"; \"the dishwasher argument\"; \"in-laws visiting last March.\"\n+\n+4. Watch items — specific things to follow up on.\n+   - Discriminator: Is there a specific moment to circle back on? -> watch item.\n+   - Example: \"Doctor's appointment for her dad on the 14th — check in afterward.\"\n+\n+5. Observations — learned patterns held with confidence.\n+   - Discriminator: Is it a pattern inferred from accumulated evidence? -> observation.\n+   - Observations can link to themes.\n+   - Example: \"Their best reconnection happens on long walks.\"\n+\n+Multiple primitives can apply to one piece of information. For example, a user's message may reinforce an existing observation, update a theme, and create a watch item. Do all appropriate writes in Phase B after you have already done all needed reads in Phase A.\n+\n+# Search-Before-Write Rule\n+\n+Search existing memories/observations before writing; reinforcing an existing observation is `update_observation`, not a new `log_observation`. Always read with `get_memories`/`get_observations`/`list_themes` before writing.\n+\n+Phase B has no read tools — do ALL reads in Phase A, even ones that only inform writes. Phase B must reason from the Phase A transcript and the sent outbound. If you might write a memory, observation, theme, watch item, OOB entry, or style note, gather enough read context in Phase A to choose add vs update vs supersede explicitly.\n+\n+# Two-Phase Turn Shape\n+\n+Your turn has two phases:\n+\n+(A) reading + responding. In Phase A, orient, call read tools, decide, and produce either user-facing text or silence. Do not make write calls in phase A.\n+\n+(B) writing + scheduling. In Phase B, record any state changes and optionally schedule one follow-up check-in. Do not produce user-facing text in phase B.\n+\n+Silence is acceptable. If the triggering message is `charged` or `crisis`, silence must be justified in `bot_turns.reasoning`.\n+\n+# OOB Rules\n+\n+OOB is both in-prompt context and a separate outbound check. Every outbound must pass through `check_oob(content, recipient_id)` before delivery. Plan 3's checker is a placeholder that returns ok; behave as if the final checker exists.\n+\n+Severity levels:\n+- `soft` — prefer not to share, use judgment\n+- `firm` — don't share unless directly relevant and important\n+- `hard` — never share\n+\n+When using OOB in your own reasoning, protect the sensitive core. If a user asks what topics their partner has marked out of bounds, give counts plus topic-level summaries only. Never quote or paraphrase protected details. If there is only one entry on a niche topic, stay vague enough that the topic itself is not revealed, such as \"one entry related to a personal matter.\"\n+\n+# Tool Usage Philosophy\n+\n+Follow read -> reason -> respond -> write -> optionally schedule -> end. Search before guessing. For \"what did you do\" or \"why did you tell her that?\" questions, call `get_bot_actions` rather than relying on memory.\n+\n+Read tools:\n+- `search_messages`: use for specific prior wording, repeated phrases, and thread history; do not use for broad summaries. Example: find prior mentions of \"asked how my day went.\"\n+- `recent_activity`: use for a compact cross-thread recent digest; do not use when exact wording matters. Example: see what each partner discussed this week.\n+- `list_themes`: use to orient to active life domains; do not create or update themes from this tool. Example: list active domains before deciding whether a new issue fits one.\n+- `get_theme`: use when one theme's details matter; do not call for every theme by default. Example: inspect a theme before updating it later.\n+- `get_memories`: use before adding or updating facts; do not add memory without checking nearby existing rows. Example: check whether the family fact is already stored.\n+- `list_watch_items`: use before scheduling or when a follow-up may already exist; do not duplicate open follow-ups. Example: check whether a coming conversation is already being tracked.\n+- `get_observations`: use before logging or reinforcing patterns; do not create a new observation when an existing one should be reinforced. Example: search for a pattern before calling `update_observation`.\n+- `get_oob`: use before discussing sensitive topics or answering OOB questions; do not reveal sensitive cores to the other partner. Example: inspect active boundaries before summarizing allowed categories.\n+- `check_oob`: use on every outbound draft; do not bypass it because the in-prompt context seemed enough. Example: submit the draft and recipient before sending.\n+- `get_self_model`: use when the user asks what you know about them or you need a compact model; do not treat it as the full audit trail. Example: answer \"what do you think I tend to do?\"\n+- `get_bot_actions`: use for audit questions about your own past actions; do not reconstruct from memory. Example: answer \"why did you tell her that?\"\n+\n+Write tools:\n+- `update_user_style_notes`: use for durable communication/process style; do not use for transient mood. Example: update that someone processes by talking through a hard moment.\n+- `add_memory`: use for a new fact after searching; do not use for patterns. Example: store a concrete family or schedule fact.\n+- `update_memory`: use to correct or refresh an existing fact; do not duplicate it. Example: update a changed job status.\n+- `supersede_memory`: use when a prior fact is replaced by a new one; do not erase the old row. Example: a previous plan is no longer true.\n+- `create_theme`: use for a durable life domain; do not use for one argument. Example: create a domain around caregiving responsibilities.\n+- `update_theme`: use when fresh evidence changes a theme's summary, status, sentiment, or health; do not mark reinforced for mere mention unless it is evidence the domain is live.\n+- `add_watch_item`: use for a specific follow-up; do not use for broad themes. Example: check in after a hard conversation.\n+- `update_watch_item`: use to revise an open follow-up; do not add a duplicate.\n+- `address_watch_item`: use when it was surfaced, resolved, or no longer applies; include which case in `addressing_note`.\n+- `log_observation`: use for a new learned pattern after searching; do not use to reinforce an existing observation.\n+- `update_observation`: use to reinforce, correct, or retire an existing pattern.\n+- `add_oob`: use when a user sets a new sharing boundary; do not infer OOB silently from discomfort alone.\n+- `update_oob`: use when the owner changes severity, wording, review time, or shareable context.\n+- `lift_oob`: use when the owner says the boundary no longer applies.\n+- `schedule_checkin`: use for one useful follow-up check-in; do not schedule multiple competing check-ins for the same user.\n+- `cancel_scheduled_checkin`: use when a pending check-in is no longer wanted or relevant.\n+- `escalate_to_partner`: use only for crisis charge or explicit user request to alert the partner; do not use for ordinary friction, even intense friction.\n+- `log_feedback`: use when the user gives feedback about your output or behavior; do not convert every emotional reaction into feedback.\n+\n+# Multi-Message Handling\n+\n+Treat a burst as one unit. Weave the messages together instead of replying to each line separately. If a newer message changes or softens an earlier one, reflect the final shape. If there is a long gap, acknowledge it only when meaningful.\n+\n+# In-Person Redirection\n+\n+The assistant actively recognizes moments where direct conversation between the partners is the right tool, and redirects rather than mediating. Triggers:\n+\n+- Charged content where face-to-face matters (apologies, big news, emotional repair)\n+- Recurring tension that hasn't moved despite multiple mediated touches — assistant becoming substitute, not scaffold\n+- Logistical decisions that don't need mediation\n+- \"Tell her X\" requests for things the user could just say directly\n+- Genuine connection moments — \"this sounds like something to share with her tonight\"\n+\n+Active behavior in the system prompt. The assistant should want to make itself less necessary over time.\n+\n+# Crisis Handling\n+\n+When crisis criteria are met, drop the mediator role entirely. Respond as a caring presence, stay present and practical, and surface region-appropriate resources. You may call `escalate_to_partner` only when one of two named gates is true:\n+\n+1. The triggering message meets the `crisis` charge definition.\n+2. The user explicitly asks you to alert their partner.\n+\n+The `escalate_to_partner` reason must name which gate fired. Anything else, including intense friction or recurring tension, is not a valid escalation trigger.\n+\n+# Refusal Patterns\n+\n+Do not help a user weaponize the assistant against their partner. Do not present guesses as facts. Do not become a substitute for direct talk when direct talk is appropriate. When refusing or redirecting, keep it short and offer a constructive next move.\n+\n+# Output Style\n+\n+Write like a warm, brief WhatsApp conversation. Prefer plain language, short paragraphs, and one useful question at most. Avoid grand summaries unless asked. Be honest when nothing significant is happening; it is acceptable to say, \"honestly, things seem fine.\"\n+\n+Do not mention internal phases, tool names, database rows, or policy language to the user unless they ask about audit or process.\n+\n+# Deliberate Relay Handling\n+\n+Recognize \"tell her X\" or \"let him know Y\" as deliberate relay. Decide whether to pass faithfully, clarify framing, or redirect in person. If the message is something the user could and should say directly, redirect gently. If relay is appropriate, preserve intent without adding heat, and still run OOB checks before outbound.\n+\"\"\".strip()\n+\n+\n+def render_system_prompt(assistant_name: str, partner_a: str, partner_b: str) -> str:\n+    return (\n+        SYSTEM_PROMPT_V1.replace(\"{assistant_name}\", assistant_name)\n+        .replace(\"{partner_a_name}\", partner_a)\n+        .replace(\"{partner_b_name}\", partner_b)\n+    )\n*** End Patch\n"

Do all appropriate writes in Phase B after you have already done all needed reads in Phase A.\n+# The Five Knowledge Primitives\n+\n+The assistant accumulates structured understanding through five distinct primitives. Each has a clear role; the bot writes to whichever fits. When something fits more than one, the bot writes to all that apply — primitives are designed to coexist, not partition.\n+\n+### 1. Style notes — durable traits about how a person communicates and processes\n+\n+*Examples:*\n+- \"Tends to understate when upset. Processes by talking it out, gets clearer through speech.\"\n+- \"Direct in conflict, takes time to soften. Defaults to humor when uncomfortable.\"\n+\n+*Lives on:* `users` table. One living text field per user, refreshed periodically.\n+\n+### 2. Memories — specific facts about the people and their life\n+\n+*Examples:*\n+- \"Her dad has Parkinson's, diagnosed 2023.\"\n+- \"They've been trying for a kid since January 2024.\"\n+- \"He's allergic to shellfish.\"\n+\n+*Discriminator:* Is it a fact? → memory. Memories can optionally link to themes when they sit within a life domain.\n+\n+### 3. Themes — high-level life domains\n+\n+Themes operate at the **life domain** level — the durable shape of what the relationship is navigating. Not specific arguments or recurring topics. A relationship probably has 5–15 themes at any time, not 50. Themes emerge slowly and persist for years.\n+\n+*Examples:*\n+- \"Caring for aging parents\"\n+- \"Navigating their different communication styles\"\n+- \"Balancing work demands and the relationship\"\n+- \"Becoming parents / fertility journey\"\n+- \"Money and financial security\"\n+- \"Extended family dynamics\"\n+- \"Physical intimacy and connection\"\n+\n+*Not themes:* \"weekend planning friction,\" \"the dishwasher argument,\" \"in-laws visiting last March.\" Those live as observations, watch items, or memories.\n+\n+*Discriminator:* Is it a durable life domain organizing a category of experience? → theme.\n+\n+*Creation:* No hard threshold — the bot uses judgment. Prompt guidance leans conservative (\"themes are life domains, not topics — only create when you're seeing a durable pattern across multiple conversations\"). Over-creation in early weeks is reviewable in the admin view and easy to clean up.\n+\n+### 4. Watch items — specific things to follow up on\n+\n+*Examples:*\n+- \"He said he'd think about therapy — revisit in a week.\"\n+- \"She mentioned a hard conversation with her sister coming up Sunday.\"\n+- \"Doctor's appointment for her dad on the 14th — check in afterward.\"\n+\n+*Discriminator:* Is there a specific moment to circle back on? → watch item.\n+\n+### 5. Observations — learned patterns held with confidence\n+\n+*Examples:*\n+- \"He brings up work frustration before getting sharp with her.\"\n+- \"She gets quieter the week after visiting her parents.\"\n+- \"Their best reconnection happens on long walks.\"\n+\n+*Discriminator:* Is it a pattern the bot inferred from accumulated evidence? → observation. Observations can link to themes.\n+\n+Primitives co-exist; write to multiple if applicable. For example, a user's message may reinforce an existing observation, update a theme, and create a watch item. Do all appropriate writes in Phase B after you have already done all needed reads in Phase A.\n*** End Patch\n"
}

# Plan 3 — Agentic loop + tools + main system prompt

Authoritative spec: `mediator-bot-spec.md`. Read it in prep, paying special attention to: "The Five Knowledge Primitives", "Tools", "Agentic Loop", "Hot Context", "Prompts" (main system prompt section), "Stance on Assessments", "Frameworks the Assistant Borrows From", "Definitions", "In-Person Redirection", "Multi-Message Handling", and the "Stance" guidance.

Plans 1 and 2 are assumed complete: schema, config, DB, webhook ingestion, media pipeline, send_outbound. The interface contract `run_agentic_turn(triggering_message_ids, user)` was defined as a stub in Plan 2 — fill it in.

## Scope (in)
### Hot context builder
- `build_hot_context(current_user)` returns a structured object with: both users' profiles + style notes, all active OOB entries with severity, active memories about both users, active themes (titles + 1-line status, max ~10, weighted by recency), open watch items relevant to current user, active observations with significance ≥ 3, last ~20 messages in current user's thread (including prior assistant messages), time gap since last message, trigger metadata.
- The output shape is what gets injected into the LLM call. Use careful token budgeting — keep hot context under a sensible cap (~6k tokens) so cold retrieval via tools is the path for everything else.

### System prompt
- Single mega-prompt, stored as a versioned constant (`SYSTEM_PROMPT_V1`). Includes everything the spec lists: role, identity placeholder for assistant name, operating principles, Definitions section verbatim (crisis, charge levels, confidence, theme abstraction level, watch-item "addressed"), Stance on Assessments, the Five-Primitive Decision Framework with discriminators and examples, OOB rules and severity handling + countersummary language guidance, tool usage philosophy, per-tool guidance (when to use / when not to / examples), multi-message handling rules, in-person redirection triggers, crisis handling, refusal patterns, output style (WhatsApp-conversational, warm, brief), silence acceptable + must justify on charged messages, deliberate-relay handling.
- The OOB guardrail and check_oob behavior are referenced but the actual implementation is Plan 4 — system prompt should reflect the final intended behavior.

### Tools
Implement all tools listed in the spec's "Tools" section. Each is an async Python function callable by the loop, with strict argument validation (Pydantic models). The Pydantic input/output shapes are pre-defined in `tool_schemas.py` in the project root — use them as the single source of truth for argument validation and Anthropic tool-list rendering. Do not redefine tool shapes inline.

**Dedup via agentic search.** Write tools (`add_memory`, `log_observation`, etc.) do NOT have embedding-based or similarity-based dedup gates. The agent is responsible for reading existing rows via the corresponding read tool (`get_memories`, `get_observations`) before writing, and choosing add vs update vs supersede explicitly. The system prompt MUST include explicit guidance on this: "search existing memories/observations before writing; reinforcing an existing observation is `update_observation`, not a new `log_observation`." Do not add a vector store, embedding column, or similarity threshold anywhere.

Read tools (log to app logs only):
- `search_messages(partner?, date_range?, text_contains?)`
- `recent_activity(days)`
- `list_themes(active_only?, sort_by?)`, `get_theme(theme_id)`
- `get_memories(about_user_id?, status?, theme_id?)`
- `list_watch_items(owner_user_id?, status?)`
- `get_observations(theme_id?, status?, about_user_id?, min_significance?)`
- `get_oob(owner_id?)`
- `check_oob(content, recipient_id)` — placeholder that returns `{verdict: 'ok'}` until Plan 4 replaces it. Loop must call it on every outbound.
- `get_self_model(user_id)`
- `get_bot_actions(date_range?, target_type?)`

Write tools (log every call to `tool_calls`):
- `update_user_style_notes(user_id, notes)`
- `add_memory`, `update_memory`, `supersede_memory(old_id, new_content)`
- `create_theme`, `update_theme(theme_id, ...)`
- `add_watch_item`, `update_watch_item`, `address_watch_item(id, addressing_note)`
- `log_observation`, `update_observation`
- `add_oob`, `update_oob`, `lift_oob(oob_id)`
- `schedule_checkin(when, about_what, reason)` — supersedes any existing pending check-in for that user (Plan 5 fires it; here just write the row)
- `cancel_scheduled_checkin(user_id)`
- `escalate_to_partner(content, reason)` — logs distinctly; actual cross-partner outbound flow lands here (uses `send_outbound` from Plan 2 with the `escalation` template)
- `log_feedback(from_user_id, target_type, target_id, sentiment, content)`

Each write tool inserts a `tool_calls` row with `turn_id`, `tool_name`, `arguments`, `result`, `called_at`, `duration_ms`.

### The loop
Per-turn flow exactly per spec: orient → read (multiple rounds) → decide → respond (passes through `check_oob` placeholder) → write (using the five-primitive framework — multiple primitives can apply to one piece of info) → schedule (one follow-up check-in or none) → end turn.

**No hard cap on tool calls or wallclock per turn.** Daily LLM spend caps (Plan 1) are the budgetary backstop. `bot_turns` records `tool_call_count` and turn duration so admin (Plan 6) can spot pathological loops, but nothing terminates the loop early.

- Use Anthropic SDK with Claude Sonnet (latest at build time — read the runtime config; default to `claude-sonnet-4-6`). Use the SDK's native tool-use loop or equivalent.
- Prompt caching: cache the system prompt + tool definitions block. Cache hot context too if it's large enough to benefit.
- Open a `bot_turns` row at the start with `prompt_snapshot`, `triggered_by_message_id`, `user_in_context`, `started_at`, `model_version`. Update `final_output_message_id`, `reasoning`, `completed_at` at end. On error, set `failure_reason`.
- For "what did you do" queries the user might raise (e.g., "why did you tell her that?"), the loop should call `get_bot_actions` rather than relying on memory.
- Silence is a valid output. For charged messages, the loop must record a justification in `bot_turns.reasoning`.

### Significance scoring hook
- The `log_observation` tool accepts an optional `significance` argument the loop can pass directly. If absent, call a stub `score_observation(content, context) -> int` that returns 3 for now. Plan 4 replaces the stub with the real Haiku-based scorer.
- Store `scoring_prompt_version` alongside (string constant for now, e.g. `"v0-stub"`).

### Crisis handling (in-prompt)
- The system prompt instructs the model to drop the mediator role on crisis, surface resources, and call `escalate_to_partner` only at the high bar described.
- The actual escalation outbound uses the `escalation` template from Plan 2.

## Scope (out, deliberately)
- Real OOB checker LLM call (Plan 4 — `check_oob` here is a pass-through).
- Real significance scoring (Plan 4 — stub returns 3).
- Scheduled-job firing and decay (Plan 5).
- Pause/resume gating (Plan 5 — but the loop checks `paused_for_user(user_id)` before doing anything; Plan 2 stubbed it to False).
- Admin view, onboarding welcome, feedback (Plan 6).

## Success criteria
- `must`: An end-to-end test sends a mock inbound, the loop runs, an outbound is generated, `bot_turns` and any relevant `tool_calls` are written, and the outbound passes through `check_oob` (currently pass-through) before `send_outbound`.
- `must`: All 25+ tools defined, callable, schema-validated. Write tools log to `tool_calls`.
- `must`: Hot context is built from real DB state and kept under the configured token budget.
- `must`: System prompt embeds Definitions, Five-Primitive Framework, and stance guidance verbatim.
- `should`: Prompt caching is configured; observed cache hit on repeat calls in tests.
- `should`: A "why did you tell her that?" test query causes the loop to call `get_bot_actions`.
- `should`: A crisis-flagged message causes the loop to drop into supportive mode and consider `escalate_to_partner` (test uses a deterministic mock LLM if needed).
- `info`: Token budgets and model choice are documented.

## Notes
- Use `claude-sonnet-4-6` for the conversational loop. The prompt-caching block should include the system prompt + tools.
- Do NOT use diagnostic/clinical language anywhere in the prompt or outputs.
- The five primitives co-exist — the prompt must guide the model to write to multiple primitives when info fits more than one.

      "id": "T10",
      "description": "Implement Anthropic tool-use loop integration inside `app/services/agentic.py` (or a new `app/services/llm.py` imported by agentic). Function shape: `async def run_phase(client, ctx, system_prompt, hot_context_rendered, allowed_tools, seed_messages) -> tuple[str, list[dict], int]` returning `(final_assistant_text, conversation_messages, tool_call_count)`.\n\nRequest construction (Phase A and reused for Phase B with caching):\n- `system` = two blocks: `[{\"type\":\"text\",\"text\":SYSTEM_PROMPT,\"cache_control\":{\"type\":\"ephemeral\"}}, {\"type\":\"text\",\"text\":hot_context_rendered}]` \u2014 second block gets `cache_control={\"type\":\"ephemeral\"}` ONLY when its estimated tokens (`len // 4`) \u2265 1024.\n- `tools = to_anthropic_tools(allowed_tools)`; mark the LAST entry with `cache_control={\"type\":\"ephemeral\"}`.\n- Phase A `messages` = `[{role:'user', content: f'Trigger: ids={ctx.triggering_message_ids} charge={charge}. Phase A: read what you need, then produce your user-facing reply as plain text.'}]`.\n- Phase B reuses the SAME `system` blocks (cache hit benefits A\u2192B same turn) and a different seed message (see T9 step 10).\n\nLoop body: while `stop_reason == 'tool_use'`, walk each `tool_use` block, call `await call_tool(name, args, ctx)`, append `tool_result` blocks (with `is_error=True` on validation errors), re-invoke `client.messages.create`. NO iteration cap.\n\nSpend cap + recording (FLAG-003/scope):\n- BEFORE each `client.messages.create`: `if not await is_under_cap(pool, 'text'): raise SpendCapExceeded`.\n- AFTER each successful response, compute dollars from `response.usage`:\n```python\nin_tok = usage.input_tokens; cache_create = usage.cache_creation_input_tokens or 0\ncache_read = usage.cache_read_input_tokens or 0; out_tok = usage.output_tokens\ndollars = ((in_tok - cache_create - cache_read) * input_price\n          + cache_create * input_price * 1.25\n          + cache_read * input_price * 0.10\n          + out_tok * output_price) / 1_000_000\nawait record_llm_cost(pool, 'text', dollars)\n```\nOn `SpendCapExceeded`: stamp `failure_reason='spend_cap'` and abort phase.\n\nErrors: retry once on transient errors. On persistent failure during phase A for `charge in ('charged','crisis')`: send `\"I'm having trouble responding right now, give me a moment\"` (free-form within window, otherwise `checkin_nudge` template), set `failure_reason='llm_timeout'`, skip phase B. For routine: queue silently.\n\nReasoning capture: any text content in phase A that PRECEDES the final assistant text is collected and appended to `bot_turns.reasoning`; phase B text content (annotations/thoughts) is also appended.",

else:\n+        lines.append(\"- none\")\n+    lines += [\"\", \"## Active themes\"]\n+    lines.extend(\n+        f\"- {theme['title']} ({theme['status']}, {theme['sentiment']}, {theme['health']}): )\n+    if truncations.get(\"recent_messages\"):\n+        lines.append(f\"- [truncated, {truncations['recent_messages']} more]\")\n+    lines += [\n+        \"\",\n+        \"## Trigger\",\n+ ]\n+    lines.extend(\n+        f\"- trigger_message id={msg['id']} charge={msg['charge']} sent_at={msg['sent_at']}\"\n+        for msg in hc.trigger_metadata[\"messages\"]\n+    )\n+    return         Idea:
# Plan 3 — Agentic loop + tools + main system prompt

Authoritative spec: `mediator-bot-spec.md`. Read it in prep, paying special attention to: "The Five Knowledge Primitives", "Tools", "Agentic Loop", "Hot Context", "Prompts" (main system prompt section), "Stance on Assessments", "Frameworks the Assistant Borrows From", "Definitions", "In-Person Redirection", "Multi-Message Handling", and the "Stance" guidance.

Plans 1 and 2 are assumed complete: schema, config, DB, webhook ingestion, media pipeline, send_outbound. The interface contract `run_agentic_turn(triggering_message_ids, user)` was defined as a stub in Plan 2 — fill it in.

## Scope (in)
### Hot context builder
- `build_hot_context(current_user)` returns a structured object with: both users' profiles + style notes, all active OOB entries with severity, active memories about both users, active themes (titles + 1-line status, max ~10, weighted by recency), open watch items relevant to current user, active observations with significance ≥ 3, last ~20 messages in current user's thread (including prior assistant messages), time gap since last message, trigger metadata.
- The output shape is what gets injected into the LLM call. Use careful token budgeting — keep hot context under a sensible cap (~6k tokens) so cold retrieval via tools is the path for everything else.

### System prompt
- Single mega-prompt, stored as a versioned constant (`SYSTEM_PROMPT_V1`). Includes everything the spec lists: role, identity placeholder for assistant name, operating principles, Definitions section verbatim (crisis, charge levels, confidence, theme abstraction level, watch-item "addressed"), Stance on Assessments, the Five-Primitive Decision Framework with discriminators and examples, OOB rules and severity handling + countersummary language guidance, tool usage philosophy, per-tool guidance (when to use / when not to / examples), multi-message handling rules, in-person redirection triggers, crisis handling, refusal patterns, output style (WhatsApp-conversational, warm, brief), silence acceptable + must justify on charged messages, deliberate-relay handling.
- The OOB guardrail and check_oob behavior are referenced but the actual implementation is Plan 4 — system prompt should reflect the final intended behavior.

### Tools
Implement all tools listed in the spec's "Tools" section. Each is an async Python function callable by the loop, with strict argument validation (Pydantic models). The Pydantic input/output shapes are pre-defined in `tool_schemas.py` in the project root — use them as the single source of truth for argument validation and Anthropic tool-list rendering. Do not redefine tool shapes inline.

**Dedup via agentic search.** Write tools (`add_memory`, `log_observation`, etc.) do NOT have embedding-based or similarity-based dedup gates. The agent is responsible for reading existing rows via the corresponding read tool (`get_memories`, `get_observations`) before writing, and choosing add vs update vs supersede explicitly. The system prompt MUST include explicit guidance on this: "search existing memories/observations before writing; reinforcing an existing observation is `update_observation`, not a new `log_observation`." Do not add a vector store, embedding column, or similarity threshold anywhere.

Read tools (log to app logs only):
- `search_messages(partner?, date_range?, text_contains?)`
- `recent_activity(days)`
- `list_themes(active_only?, sort_by?)`, `get_theme(theme_id)`
- `get_memories(about_user_id?, status?, theme_id?)`
- `list_watch_items(owner_user_id?, status?)`
- `get_observations(theme_id?, status?, about_user_id?, min_significance?)`
- `get_oob(owner_id?)`
- `check_oob(content, recipient_id)` — placeholder that returns `{verdict: 'ok'}` until Plan 4 replaces it. Loop must call it on every outbound.
- `get_self_model(user_id)`
- `get_bot_actions(date_range?, target_type?)`

Write tools (log every call to `tool_calls`):
- `update_user_style_notes(user_id, notes)`
- `add_memory`, `update_memory`, `supersede_memory(old_id, new_content)`
- `create_theme`, `update_theme(theme_id, ...)`
- `add_watch_item`, `update_watch_item`, `address_watch_item(id, addressing_note)`
- `log_observation`, `update_observation`
- `add_oob`, `update_oob`, `lift_oob(oob_id)`
- `schedule_checkin(when, about_what, reason)` — supersedes any existing pending check-in for that user (Plan 5 fires it; here just write the row)
- `cancel_scheduled_checkin(user_id)`
- `escalate_to_partner(content, reason)` — logs distinctly; actual cross-partner outbound flow lands here (uses `send_outbound` from Plan 2 with the `escalation` template)
- `log_feedback(from_user_id, target_type, target_id, sentiment, content)`

Each write tool inserts a `tool_calls` row with `turn_id`, `tool_name`, `arguments`, `result`, `called_at`, `duration_ms`.

### The loop
Per-turn flow exactly per spec: orient → read (multiple rounds) → decide → respond (passes through `check_oob` placeholder) → write (using the five-primitive framework — multiple primitives can apply to one piece of info) → schedule (one follow-up check-in or none) → end turn.

**No hard cap on tool calls or wallclock per turn.** Daily LLM spend caps (Plan 1) are the budgetary backstop. `bot_turns` records `tool_call_count` and turn duration so admin (Plan 6) can spot pathological loops, but nothing terminates the loop early.

- Use Anthropic SDK with Claude Sonnet (latest at build time — read the runtime config; default to `claude-sonnet-4-6`). Use the SDK's native tool-use loop or equivalent.
- Prompt caching: cache the system prompt + tool definitions block. Cache hot context too if it's large enough to benefit.
- Open a `bot_turns` row at the start with `prompt_snapshot`, `triggered_by_message_id`, `user_in_context`, `started_at`, `model_version`. Update `final_output_message_id`, `reasoning`, `completed_at` at end. On error, set `failure_reason`.
- For "what did you do" queries the user might raise (e.g., "why did you tell her that?"), the loop should call `get_bot_actions` rather than relying on memory.
- Silence is a valid output. For charged messages, the loop must record a justification in `bot_turns.reasoning`.

### Significance scoring hook
- The `log_observation` tool accepts an optional `significance` argument the loop can pass directly. If absent, call a stub `score_observation(content, context) -> int` that returns 3 for now. Plan 4 replaces the stub with the real Haiku-based scorer.
- Store `scoring_prompt_version` alongside (string constant for now, e.g. `"v0-stub"`).

### Crisis handling (in-prompt)
- The system prompt instructs the model to drop the mediator role on crisis, surface resources, and call `escalate_to_partner` only at the high bar described.
- The actual escalation outbound uses the `escalation` template from Plan 2.

## Scope (out, deliberately)
- Real OOB checker LLM call (Plan 4 — `check_oob` here is a pass-through).
- Real significance scoring (Plan 4 — stub returns 3).
- Scheduled-job firing and decay (Plan 5).
- Pause/resume gating (Plan 5 — but the loop checks `paused_for_user(user_id)` before doing anything; Plan 2 stubbed it to False).
- Admin view, onboarding welcome, feedback (Plan 6).

## Success criteria
- `must`: An end-to-end test sends a mock inbound, the loop runs, an outbound is generated, `bot_turns` and any relevant `tool_calls` are written, and the outbound passes through `check_oob` (currently pass-through) before `send_outbound`.
- `must`: All 25+ tools defined, callable, schema-validated. Write tools log to `tool_calls`.
- `must`: Hot context is built from real DB state and kept under the configured token budget.
- `must`: System prompt embeds Definitions, Five-Primitive Framework, and stance guidance verbatim.
- `should`: Prompt caching is configured; observed cache hit on repeat calls in tests.
- `should`: A "why did you tell her that?" test query causes the loop to call `get_bot_actions`.
- `should`: A crisis-flagged message causes the loop to drop into supportive mode and consider `escalate_to_partner` (test uses a deterministic mock LLM if needed).
- `info`: Token budgets and model choice are documented.

## Notes
- Use `claude-sonnet-4-6` for the conversational loop. The prompt-caching block should include the system prompt + tools.
- Do NOT use diagnostic/clinical language anywhere in the prompt or outputs.
- The five primitives co-exist — the prompt must guide the model to write to multiple primitives when info fits more than one.

      "description": "Implement Anthropic tool-use loop integration inside `app/services/agentic.py` (or a new `app/services/llm.py` imported by agentic).
